module_title: Radioactivity, Alpha, Beta, Gamma Rays, and Half-Life
introduction: Some atomic nuclei are unstable. To become stable, they spontaneously emit invisible, high-energy particles and rays. This natural phenomenon is called Radioactivity.

core_concepts.title: Discovery of Radioactivity
core_concepts.description: Radioactivity was discovered accidentally by 'Henri Becquerel' in 1896 while working with Uranium. Later, Marie Curie and Pierre Curie discovered the highly radioactive elements Radium and Polonium.

core_concepts.title: Types of Radioactive Emissions
core_concepts.description:
1. Alpha Rays ($\alpha$): Positively charged Helium nuclei ($^4_2\text{He}$). Heavy and slow. 
2. Beta Rays ($\beta$): Fast-moving electrons ($e^-$). Negatively charged and lighter. 
3. Gamma Rays ($\gamma$): Pure electromagnetic waves (Photons). No mass, no charge. They travel at the speed of light.

core_concepts.title: Penetrating vs. Ionizing Power
core_concepts.description:
1. Penetrating Power (Ability to pass through matter): $\gamma > \beta > \alpha$. (Gamma can pass through thick lead; Alpha is stopped by paper). 
2. Ionizing Power (Ability to knock electrons off other atoms): $\alpha > \beta > \gamma$. (Alpha is highly damaging if ingested).

core_concepts.title: Half-Life Period ($T_{1/2}$)
core_concepts.description:
The time required for exactly HALF of the unstable nuclei in a radioactive sample to decay. 
Example: If Carbon-14 has a half-life of 5,730 years, 100 grams of C-14 will reduce to 50 grams after 5,730 years, and then to 25 grams after another 5,730 years.

important_entities.name: Carbon Dating (C-14)
important_entities.significance: The isotope Carbon-14 is used to determine the age of once-living things (fossils, wood, bones). For non-living rocks and the Earth itself, 'Uranium Dating' is used.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Exam Trap: 'Who discovered Radioactivity?' Students often jump to Madame Curie. FALSE. Henri Becquerel discovered radioactivity. Curie coined the term and discovered specific radioactive elements.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Gamma has no body (mass) and no charge, but walks through walls.
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Helps you remember that Gamma rays have the highest penetrating power but zero mass and charge.

exam_strategy_tips: Railway Exams often ask: 'Which ray is deflected towards the positive plate in an electric field?' Answer: Beta rays (because they are negatively charged electrons).
